assessment.title: Ecosystem Interactions Assessment
assessment.subject: Biology
assessment.description: Assessment on ecosystem interactions and food web dynamics

studentResponse: {"rawAnswer":{"explanationQuestion":"Ecosystems are complex networks of interactions between living organisms and their environment. I've learned that food webs illustrate energy flow through trophic levels, with producers converting sunlight into chemical energy, primary consumers eating producers, and secondary consumers eating primary consumers. Decomposers play a crucial role by breaking down dead organic matter and recycling nutrients back into the ecosystem. Keystone species have disproportionate effects on ecosystem structure and function.","observationQuestion":"During our field study of the forest ecosystem, I conducted a biodiversity survey and observed fascinating interactions. I counted 15 different plant species, 8 bird species, and 5 mammal species. I noticed that the removal of a single large oak tree would affect multiple species - birds lost nesting sites, squirrels lost food sources, and fungi lost their substrate. This demonstrated the interconnectedness of ecosystem components."}}
